title: Senior Applied Research Economist
description:
Hiring Department

Rural & Farm Finance Policy Analysis Center (RaFF) - Division
of Applied Social Sciences

Job Description

This Senior Applied Research Economist position combines applied
economic research with leadership of the Early Warning System of
Farm Financial Stress (EWS). This role will advance RaFF's research
and stakeholder engagement activities focused on farm financial
conditions, agricultural lending, and financial stress in the farm
sector.

The role develops analytical tools and models, conducts applied
research on farm finance and agricultural credit markets, and leads
EWS activities across participating states. Working with producers,
lenders, policymakers, researchers, and Extension professionals,
the position integrates economic analysis and stakeholder
intelligence to identify emerging risks and deliver actionable
insights that support decision-making across the agricultural
finance sector.

Responsibilities

Lead the implementation and improvement of the Early Warning
System of Farm Financial Stress (EWS).
Engage producers, lenders, Extension professionals,
researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders to monitor
emerging financial risks and conditions.
Coordinate EWS stakeholder meetings, manage project activities,
and oversee development of consensus reports and related
outputs.
Synthesize stakeholder input, economic data, and analytical
findings into reports, presentations, and decision-support
materials.
Develop and enhance models used for farm income projections,
agricultural lending analysis, farm financial stress assessment,
and policy evaluation.
Conduct applied research on farm finance, agricultural credit
markets, and related policy issues.
Contribute to Farm Income Outlook reports, Missouri
Agricultural Outlook publications, and other RaFF products.
Present findings to policymakers, producers, lenders, industry
groups, and professional audiences.
Lead collaborative projects and pursue external funding
opportunities that support RaFF's mission.
Mentor graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and research
staff as appropriate.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Knowledge of U.S. agricultural policy, commodity markets, farm
finance, and agricultural lending.
Experience conducting applied economic analysis and developing
decision-support tools.
Ability to integrate quantitative analysis with stakeholder
input to assess emerging conditions and risks.
Experience leading collaborative projects and stakeholder
engagement activities.
Quality and impact of applied research, policy analysis,
reports, and presentations.
Strong written and oral communication skills for technical and
non-technical audiences.

Shift

Monday - Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and
relevant experience, and at least 5 years of experience from which
comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

PhD in Agricultural Economics, Applied Economics, Economics, or
a related field with 2+ years of post-PhD experience; OR Master's
degree with 5+ years of relevant experience; OR Bachelor's degree
with 10+ years of relevant experience.
Deep knowledge of agricultural markets, farm finance,
agricultural credit systems, and agricultural policy.
Experience with applied economic modeling, econometrics,
forecasting, or policy analysis.
Experience leading stakeholder engagement, consensus-building
processes, or multi-state initiatives.
Proficiency with R, Excel, and other analytical software.
Experience managing research projects and mentoring graduate
students, postdoctoral fellows or research staff.¿

Other Information

The Rural and Farm Finance Policy Analysis Center (RaFF) at the
University of Missouri provides objective policy analysis and
informs decision-makers on issues affecting farm and rural
finances. We use data from many sources to estimate how policy
decisions, innovations, and other events affect the ability of
farmers and ranchers to make a profit. Cooperation with
participating states brings local expertise to enhance model design
and estimates. This results in customized, state-level economic
models and policy analyses for regions across the U.S. Learn more
at raff.missouri.edu .

Community Information

Columbia offers small-town friendliness with big city features and

Founded on education and known as an ideal college town, its
location also makes it an attractive spot for businesses and
travelers. Located on Interstate 70 and U.S. Highway 63, Columbia

hours’ drive from St. Louis and Kansas City, Columbia is Boone
County’s largest population center offering big-city culture,
activities, and resources with a low cost of living. Columbia is
home to a variety of restaurants and entertainment venues and hosts
more than a dozen festivals each year. If you want to grow your
career, continue your education, raise a family, and retire,
Columbia is a good place to be!
